result.title: VidToC: Rethinking Video Token Compression for Multimodal Large Language Models
result.summary: Extending multimodal large language models (MLLMs) from images to videos faces substantial memory and latency challenges due to the massive number of visual tokens. These challenges have driven the development of numerous visual token compression methods and more efficient LLM architectures. However, existing compression methods are often evaluated with different training setups, tasks, and models, making fair comparison difficult. Meanwhile, the growing use of hybrid Mamba-Transformer architectures raises questions about whether compression strategies transfer across backbones. We present VidToC, a controlled evaluation framework for representative compression algorithms, LLM backbones, and time encoding strategies, covering training-free and fine-tuned settings on three complementary video understanding tasks. Our results reveal task-dependent compression behavior and characterize the effects of compression placement, time encoding, and backbone choice. These findings provide empirical guidance for designing and selecting video token compression strategies across tasks and training settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VidToC 受控评测框架，在三种视频理解任务上统一比较代表性视觉 token 压缩算法，并考察压缩位置、时间编码策略与 Transformer/Mamba 混合骨干在免训练和微调设定下的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 压缩本质上决定保留哪些视觉证据，其任务依赖的压缩行为可供核查视觉信息坍缩如何影响多模态推理所需细节与计算节省；但未涉及 latent 推理状态或 THINK/LOOK/STOP 决策，需读原文确认是否分析推理类任务。
